review_notes:
I read the whole file and the definitions it depends on: `CircleAction` (CircleFourier.lean), `HilbertFlow`, `timeIntegral` and `HasGenerator` (HilbertFlow.lean). `HilbertFlow` and `CircleAction` are structures defined in other files, not in the target. They are domain-specific bundles of a strongly continuous unitary action. `HasGenerator` is an integral-form generator graph whose rationale is documented ("immediate linear-test fact"). I found no matching Mathlib concept that would justify consolidation, and I did not search Mathlib for one.

The new declarations in this file are `angularCircleAction` (an instance of the repo's own structure), `angularProjection`, `circlePeriodPositive`, `RotationalCR`, and several lemmas. `RotationalCR` is a billiard-specific predicate and has no Mathlib counterpart. The lemmas (`HasGenerator.add`, `smul`, `integral`, the rotation decompositions) are theorem-level, which the rubric excludes.

The one borderline item is `circlePeriodPositive`, a global `Fact (0 < 2 * Real.pi)` instance. The same fact is re-declared as a local instance in many sibling files and elsewhere in the repo. Mathlib has no global instance for it. The only match is a `local instance` in Mathlib/Analysis/Polynomial/Fourier.lean. So this is not a competing version of a Mathlib concept, and I am not reporting it.

Remaining uncertainty: I did not search Mathlib for a generic strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group or semigroup-generator notion. I do not expect Mathlib to have one, but I did not rule it out.
